main_body: A farm ground patch: golden crop rows on top, a grass fringe, then tilled brown soil with sprouts. It is a flat terrain tile block, not a standing object.
top_band: none (terrain tile; the column reads as crop texture rows 0-14, grass rows 16-19, soil below, with no standing-object top band)
evidence: The kind is terrain, so the standing-object 3/4 contract does not apply. The drawing is a ground surface patch with horizontal bands of crop, grass and soil. It has no standing body, no isometric side faces and no front-elevation object. It passes as terrain.

style.evidence: The candidate has 13 median colours per tile and 23 distinct colours, against 26 and 80 for the grass reference and 7 and 7 for the paving reference. That is lower than grass but above paving. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, and the dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines are tinted brown and green rather than near-black. Texture is dense: speckled crop rows, grass tufts and soil grain with sprouts, with about 5 lightness steps in the greens and browns. It is somewhat less varied than the grass reference in colour count, but it is structurally rich and not sticker-like. I judge it acceptable beside the references.
